Since [MATH: PM=PO], it is an isosceles triangle with the base [MATH: \overline{MO}.] So, the base angles are equal: [MATH: m\angle M = m\angle O]

The sum of the measures of the interior angles of a triangle is [MATH: 180^\circ.] For [MATH: \triangle MPO,] this gives

[MATH: m∠MPO + m∠M + m∠O|= 180^{∘}; 132^{∘} + m∠O + m∠O|= 180^{∘}; 132^{∘} + 2m∠O|= 180^{∘}; 2m∠O|= 48^{∘}; m∠O|= 24^{∘}.]

Now, consider [MATH: \triangle ONQ.]

Using again that the sum of the measures of the interior angles of a triangle is [MATH: 180^\circ,] we get

[MATH: m∠ONQ + m∠O + m∠Q|= 180^{∘}; m∠ONQ + 24^{∘} + 19^{∘}|= 180^{∘}; m∠ONQ + 43^{∘}|= 180^{∘}; m∠ONQ|= 137^{∘}.]

Finally, since [MATH: \angle MON] is a straight angle and [MATH: m\angle ONQ=137^\circ,] we have

[MATH: m∠QNM + m∠ONQ|= 180^{∘}; x^{∘} + 137^{∘}|= 180^{∘}; x^{∘}|= 43^{∘}.]

Therefore, the value of [MATH: x] is [MATH: 43.]
